requirement: Parse robot command lines into Move and Say values with a match statement over the split tokens, defaulting moves to one step, rejecting unknown commands and bad step counts with ValueError, and run a list of commands to a final position and the spoken lines.
skeleton: DIRECTIONS table, frozen Move and Say dataclasses, parse matching sequence patterns with guards and a wildcard fallback, and run matching class patterns on each parsed command.
caption: A robot command language written with Python structural pattern matching. DIRECTIONS maps north, south, east and west to unit dx and dy offsets. Move and Say are frozen dataclasses from the dataclasses module. parse(line) matches line.split(), so runs of whitespace collapse, against sequence patterns: move with a known direction is one step; move with a known direction and a step count raises ValueError saying bad step count unless the count is all digits and at least 1, and otherwise scales the offset; say with at least one word, captured by a star pattern with an if words guard, joins the words with single spaces; and the wildcard case raises ValueError saying unknown command with the line. Guards on the direction keep unknown directions out of the dictionary lookup. run(lines) starts at the origin and matches each parsed command with class patterns Move(dx=dx, dy=dy), adding the offset to the position, and Say(text=text), collecting the text, then returns the final position and the spoken lines. The fixture asserts moves with and without steps, collapsed whitespace, ValueError for say alone, move up 3, jump, an empty line and too many tokens, ValueError for step counts 0, x and -2, and that a five-line script ends at (2, 2) having said hi and bye now.

plan.intent: Interpret a small robot command language
constraints: move takes a known direction and an optional positive step count
say needs at least one word and joins words with single spaces
Repeated whitespace between tokens is ignored
Unknown commands and unknown directions raise ValueError
Step counts that are not positive integers raise ValueError
run adds every move to the position and collects spoken text in order

rationale.teaches: match with sequence patterns, star captures and guards for parsing, and keyword class patterns for dispatching on dataclasses.
rationale.why: Missing guards let an empty star capture or an unknown key fall through to the wrong branch, and those inputs rarely appear in happy-path examples.

ops.docstring: Parse and run robot commands with structural pattern matching.

ops.source:
def run(lines: Iterable[str]) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], list[str]]:
    """Run commands from the origin; return the final position and spoken text."""
    x = y = 0
    spoken: list[str] = []
    for line in lines:
        match parse(line):
            case Move(dx=dx, dy=dy):
                x, y = x + dx, y + dy
            case Say(text=text):
                spoken.append(text)
    return (x, y), spoken

candidates.why_wrong: A bare say matches the star pattern with no words and produces an empty Say.
Without the direction guard an unknown direction reaches the dict lookup and raises KeyError.
A step count of zero is accepted and produces a move that goes nowhere.
Splitting on a single space keeps empty tokens, so repeated spaces break every pattern.
Each move replaces the position instead of adding to it, so earlier moves are lost.
